title: Minimum Cost to Make Array Equalindromic
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, you can perform a special move any number of times.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, you can perform a special move any number of times. In one move, choose an index i and a positive integer x, add the absolute difference between nums[i] and x to the total cost, and then set nums[i] to x. A palindromic number reads the same backward as forward. An array is equalindromic if all elements are equal to a palindromic number y less than 10^9. Find the minimum total cost to make nums equalindromic.
constraints: Choose one positive palindromic integer target.
Return the minimum sum of absolute changes needed to make every nums value equal to that target.
hints: Without the palindrome restriction, absolute distance is minimized at a median.
Generate palindromes and check the nearest candidates around the median.
Binary-search the median in the sorted palindrome list and evaluate neighboring targets.
The convex absolute-distance objective cannot improve after moving past the closest feasible target on either side.
editorial: The convex absolute-distance objective cannot improve after moving past the closest feasible target on either side.

tests.explanation: Target three is palindromic and gives total cost six.
The best palindromic target near the median minimizes total absolute distance.
